content: The provided text is a detailed and technical document, primarily focused on pathology reporting, laboratory standards, and cancer staging. 1. Specimen Dimensions: The number of tissue pieces and their individual dimensions should be recorded for each piece. For loop or cone biopsies, the dimensions of the ectocervix and the depth of the specimen should be noted. For trachelectomy and hysterectomy specimens, the vaginal cuff's minimum and maximum lengths, as well as the lateral extent of the left and right parametria, should be documented. 2. Macroscopic Appearance of Tumor(s): Tumors may present as exophytic/polypoid, flat, ulcerated, or circumferential/barrel-shaped. If no macroscopic tumor is visible, this should be explicitly stated. 3. Patient and Specimen Identification: Essential details include the patient’s family name, given name(s), identifiers, date of request, and accession/laboratory number. Core elements are mandatory, while non-core elements are optional. 4. Scope of Dataset: This dataset applies to loop excision procedures, including LEEP (Loop Electrosurgical Excision Procedure) and LLETZ (Large Loop Excision of the Transformation Zone). It also applies to trachelectomy and hysterectomy specimens. 5. Tumor Dimensions: For separate tumors, dimensions should be specified individually. Horizontal extent and depth of invasion should be measured, with the phrase at least included if the tumor is present at a resection margin. 6. Lymph Node Status: If lymph nodes are not submitted or cannot be assessed due to fragmentation, this should be indicated. 7. Provisional Pathological Staging (FIGO 2018): Stage I: Carcinoma confined to the cervix uteri. IA: Invasive carcinoma diagnosed microscopically with a depth of invasion <5 mm. IA1: Stromal invasion <3 mm. IA2: Stromal invasion ≥3 mm but <5 mm. IB: Invasive carcinoma with a depth of invasion ≥5 mm, limited to the cervix. IB1: Depth ≥5 mm and <2 cm in greatest dimension. IB2: Dimension ≥2 cm and <4 cm. IB3: Dimension ≥4 cm. Stage II: Carcinoma extends beyond the uterus but not to the lower third of the vagina or pelvic wall. IIA: Involvement limited to the upper two-thirds of the vagina without parametrial involvement. IIA1: Tumor <4 cm. IIA2: Tumor ≥4 cm. IIB: Parametrial involvement without extension to the pelvic wall. Stage III: Carcinoma involves the lower third of the vagina, pelvic wall, or causes hydronephrosis/non-functioning kidney. IIIA: Involves the lower third of the vagina without pelvic wall extension. IIIB: Extends to the pelvic wall or causes hydronephrosis/non-functioning kidney. IIIC: Pelvic and/or para-aortic lymph node involvement. IIIC1: Pelvic lymph node metastasis only. IIIC2: Para-aortic lymph node metastasis. Stage IV: Carcinoma extends beyond the true pelvis or involves the mucosa of the bladder or rectum. 8. TNM Staging (UICC 8th Edition): Tumor (T): T1: Confined to the cervix. T2: Extends beyond the cervix but not to the pelvic wall or lower third of the vagina. T2b: With parametrial invasion. T3: Extends to the pelvic wall, involves the lower third of the vagina, or causes hydronephrosis/non-functioning kidney. T3a: Involves the lower third of the vagina. T3b: Extends to the pelvic wall or causes hydronephrosis/non-functioning kidney. T4: Invades the mucosa of the bladder or rectum or extends beyond the true pelvis. Nodes (N): NX: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed. N0: No regional lymph node metastasis. N1: Regional lymph node metastasis. 9. Laboratory Standards: Laboratories should maintain a safe and adequate working environment, with proper separation of incompatible activities, clean work areas, and appropriate ventilation. Essential equipment must be functional, with preventive maintenance programs in place. Supplies and reagents should be adequately stocked, with proper inventory management to avoid shortages. 10. Quality Management: Laboratories must have a documented quality management system, with regular internal and external audits. Staff should be trained and authorized to use equipment, and continuing education programs should be available. 11. Pathology Reporting: Results must be reported in a standardized format, reviewed, and authorized before release. Critical results should be immediately communicated to physicians. 12. Waste Management: Biomedical waste disposal should follow established guidelines, with SOPs for spill management and staff training. 13. Accreditation and Audits: Laboratories should aim for accreditation and undergo regular audits to ensure compliance with international standards. This version retains the technical details while presenting the information in a clear, professional, and structured manner suitable for medical professionals.
